<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" />{{rh|160|THE GOSPEL|CHA. VIII.}}</noinclude>my brethren, are they that heare the vvord of God and doe it.

{{verse|chapter=8|verse=22}}† {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Mat. 8, 23. Mar. 4, 36.''}}* And it came to passe one day: and he vvent vp into a boate, and his disciples, and he said to them, Let vs strike ouer the lake. And they launched forth. {{verse|chapter=8|verse=23}}† And vvhen they vvere sailing, he slept: and there fel a storme of vvinde into the lake, and they {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=∷ ''c complebantur.''}}∷ vvere filled, and vvere in danger. {{verse|chapter=8|verse=24}}† And {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=∷ See the Annotations vpon S. Matthew c. 8, 24.}}∷ they came and raised him, saying, Maister, vve perish. But he rising, rebuked the vvinde and the tempest of vvater: and it ceased, and there vvas made a calme. {{verse|chapter=8|verse=25}}† And he said to them, VVhere is your faith? Who fearing, marueiled one to an other, saying, VVho is this (trovv ye) that he commaundeth both the vvindes and the sea, and they obey him? {{verse|chapter=8|verse=26}}† {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Mt. 8, 28. Mr. 5, 1.''}}* And they sailed to the countrie of the Gerasens vvhich is ouer against Galilee.

{{verse|chapter=8|verse=27}}† And vvhen he vvas come forth to the land, there mette him a certaine man that had a deuil novv a very long time, and he did vveare no clothes, neither did he tarie in house, but in the monuments. {{verse|chapter=8|verse=28}}† And as he saw {{sc|Iesvs}}, he fel dovvne before him: and crying out vvith a great voice, he said, VVhat is to me and thee {{sc|Iesvs}} sonne of God most high? I beseech thee doe not torment me. {{verse|chapter=8|verse=29}}† For he commaunded the vncleane spirit to goe forth out of the man. For many times he caught him, and he was bound vvith chaines, and kept vvith fetters: and breaking the bondes vvas driuen of the deuil into the deserts. {{verse|chapter=8|verse=30}}† And {{sc|Iesvs}} asked him saying, VVhat is thy name? But he said, Legion. because many deuils vvere entred into him. {{verse|chapter=8|verse=31}}† And they besought him that he vvould not commaund them to goe into the depth. {{verse|chapter=8|verse=32}}† And there vvas there a heard of many svvine feeding on the mountaine: and they desired him, that he vvould permit them to enter into them. And he permitted them. {{verse|chapter=8|verse=33}}† The deuils therfore vvent forth out of the man, and entred into the swine: and the heard vvith violence vvent headlong into the lake, and vvas stifled. {{verse|chapter=8|verse=34}}† Which vvhen the svvineheards savv done, they fled: and told into the citie and into the tovvnes. {{verse|chapter=8|verse=35}}† And they vvent forth to see that vvhich vvas done: and they came to {{sc|Iesvs}}, and found the man, out of whom the deuils vvere gone forth, sitting at his feete, clothed, and vvel in his vvittes, and they vvere afraid. {{verse|chapter=8|verse=36}}† And they also that had seen, told them hovv he had been made whole from the legion. {{verse|chapter=8|verse=37}}† And al the multitude of the countrie of the Gerasens besought him to depart from<noinclude>{{rh|||them:}}</noinclude>
